author: feral-core
description: Unified personal-health view across the platforms the user has connected: Whoop (recovery, strain, sleep, HRV, resting heart rate), Oura (readiness, sleep, activity), Apple HealthKit (heart rate, sleep, workouts (paired iPhone, ingested via the FERAL companion app), AND live wearable sensors that stream directly into the brain (Theora smart glasses, BLE wristbands: heart rate, SpO2, skin temperature). Use this skill any time the user asks about sleep, recovery, readiness, heart rate, HRV, strain, activity, or week-over-week vitals trends. It merges whatever sources are connected, tags each data point with its source, and falls back to the glasses-derived vitals trend when no third-party wearable is connected.
trigger_phrases: how was my sleep last night
what was my heart rate this morning
how were my vitals this week
how were my vitals over the last week
my recovery over the last six months
my recovery over the last year
how has my resting heart rate changed

endpoints.description: Single-call snapshot of the user's biometrics: sleep_hours, sleep_quality, recovery_score, resting_hr, hrv (ms), readiness, activity_score, strain, current_hr and current_spo2 with their sources. Resting heart rate is null unless a rest-qualified source provides it; a live reading is current_hr, not resting_hr. Each unavailable field is null; the response lists contributing platforms in 'sources'. Any vitals_trend resting_hr_estimate is a historical-minimum heuristic, not a qualified resting measurement. Read-only.
endpoints.returns_description: {sleep_hours, sleep_quality, recovery_score, resting_hr, hrv, readiness, activity_score, strain, current_hr, current_hr_source, current_spo2, current_spo2_source, sources, vitals_trend?}

endpoints.description: Per-day sleep entries from every connected platform over the past N days. Each entry is tagged with its 'source_name' (the product name to use when speaking) so the LLM can describe convergence or divergence between platforms. Read-only.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back from today to include (default 7).

endpoints.returns_description: Array of {date, total_sleep_hours, sleep_score, source} entries, sorted ascending by date.

endpoints.description: Per-day recovery / readiness scores from every connected platform over the past N days. Whoop contributes a 'strain' value, Oura contributes 'readiness'; both are returned in the same shape with a 'type' field so the LLM can describe each correctly. Read-only.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back from today to include (default 7).

endpoints.returns_description: Array of {date, score, type: 'strain'|'readiness', source} entries, sorted ascending by date.

endpoints.description: Week-over-week vitals trend derived from live wearable sensors that stream directly into the brain (Theora smart glasses, BLE wristbands), NOT third-party cloud platforms. Use this for 'how were my vitals this week / over the last week', resting heart-rate trend, HR range, or SpO2 trend when the user has no Whoop/Oura/HealthKit connected. Returns per-day resting-HR (daily min), avg/max HR, SpO2 avg/min, sample counts, and the contributing source(s). Also the most recent BLOOD PRESSURE reading under 'blood_pressure' (systolic, diastolic, mmHg, measured_at, age_seconds) when one has been taken: the glasses measure BP on demand rather than streaming it, so use this for 'what was my blood pressure' and always report the pair together with when it was measured. Honest about provenance ('derived from glasses sensor, N samples over Nd'). Read-only.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back from today to include (default 7).

endpoints.returns_description: {window_days, sources, primary_source, hr_sample_count, spo2_sample_count, resting_hr_trend: [{date, resting_hr, avg_hr, max_hr, samples}], hr_range: {min,max,avg}, spo2_avg, spo2_min, resting_hr_estimate, note}

endpoints.description: Long-window health history read straight out of the brain's durable biometric store, NOT from a vendor API. This is the endpoint for questions that span months: 'my recovery over the last six months', 'how has my resting heart rate changed since spring', 'my sleep this year'. Whoop's daily records (recovery, resting HR, HRV, sleep hours/score/efficiency/REM/deep, respiratory rate, strain, avg and max HR, energy) are mirrored into that store on a schedule, so this works even while Whoop is unreachable and it reaches far further back than sleep_trend or recovery_trend, which only query the vendor's last N days. Live wearable samples (Theora glasses, BLE wristbands) are in the same store. Every entry is tagged with a 'source_name'. Read-only. Blood pressure is stored here as two paired metrics, 'bp_systolic' and 'bp_diastolic', sharing one timestamp; quote them together, never one alone.

params.name: days
params.description: How many days back from today to include (default 180).

params.name: metric
params.description: Restrict to one canonical metric: recovery_score, resting_hr, hrv, sleep_hours, sleep_score, sleep_efficiency, rem_hours, deep_hours, respiratory_rate, strain, avg_hr, max_hr, calories_kj, spo2_avg, skin_temp_avg, hr, spo2, skin_temp, steps. Omit for every metric with data in the window.

endpoints.returns_description: {window_days, metrics: [...], sources: [...], sample_count, series: {metric: [{metric, label, value, unit, precision, category, source, ts}]}, note}

flows.description: Morning briefing: pull current snapshot then last 7 days of sleep + recovery for context
